question: Which externally supported techniques best address G01 entity-reranker gains and regressions?

sources.title: Found in the Middle: Permutation Self-Consistency Improves Listwise Ranking in Large Language Models
sources.borrow: counterbalanced candidate orders and central-ranking aggregation
sources.boundary: passage and sorting results do not establish G01 effectiveness

sources.title: Position Bias Undermines Preference Consistency in Listwise LLM-Based Reranking
sources.borrow: measure pairwise, global, and output instability under equivalent permutations
sources.boundary: recommendation experiments motivate a diagnostic only

sources.title: Large Language Models are Effective Text Rankers with Pairwise Ranking Prompting
sources.borrow: bounded pairwise comparisons when listwise consensus is insufficient
sources.boundary: pairwise cost must be bounded for G01

sources.title: PRP-Graph: Pairwise Ranking Prompting to LLMs with Graph Aggregation for Effective Text Re-ranking
sources.borrow: aggregate pairwise preferences as a ranking graph
sources.boundary: requires a separately frozen comparison schedule

sources.title: RGFL: Reasoning Guided Fault Localization for Automated Program Repair Using Large Language Models
sources.borrow: bug-specific candidate evidence and two-stage graph/model ranking
sources.boundary: reported SWE-bench results are not transferable to BugSwarm

sources.title: Boosting Bug-Report-Oriented Fault Localization with Segmentation and Stack-Trace Analysis
sources.borrow: one query-matched source segment and explicit stack-trace treatment
sources.boundary: G01 entity cards already partially realize this mechanism

sources.title: ARISE: A Repository-level Graph Representation and Toolset for Agentic Program Repair and Fault Localization
sources.borrow: statement-level definition-use edges and data-flow slicing
sources.boundary: deferred because two-language construction exceeds the next experiment

sources.title: Reciprocal Rank Fusion outperforms Condorcet and individual Rank Learning Methods
sources.borrow: fixed k=60 unsupervised fusion of the graph prior and counterbalanced GLM rankings
sources.boundary: IR results motivate a gold-blind aggregation candidate; they do not establish G01 effectiveness

sources.title: Beyond Sampling: Self-Sorting for Long-Context Ranking
sources.borrow: selection-time comparison of multiple candidate rankings and joint within-list/cross-list scoring
sources.boundary: requires extra model calls and a prospectively fixed lambda; retain as escalation after simple fusion

sources.title: Batched Self-Consistency Improves LLM Relevance Assessment and Ranking
sources.borrow: diversified shuffled batches and repeated black-box scoring without one call per candidate
sources.boundary: published gains use retrieval datasets and up to 15 stochastic calls; G01 needs a much smaller fixed budget

sources.title: LLM-RankFusion: Mitigating Intrinsic Inconsistency in LLM-based Ranking
sources.borrow: measure order reversal and transitivity failures, then restrict pairwise comparison to the disagreement frontier
sources.boundary: the exact probability calibration may require model signals absent from the current GLM transport

sources.title: Learning from Emptiness: De-biasing Listwise Rerankers with Content-Agnostic Probability Calibration
sources.borrow: content-free estimation of intrinsic positional priors
sources.boundary: not currently transport-compatible because CapCal requires output logits and the ARE GLM contract exposes messages, tools, parsed output, and usage only

sources.title: CoSIL: Software Issue Localization via LLM-Driven Code Repository Graph Searching
sources.borrow: iterative module/function graph traversal with explicit context pruning
sources.boundary: changes candidate generation and evidence supply, so it belongs in a separate graph-search hypothesis after reranking is stabilized

sources.title: AgentFL: Scaling LLM-based Fault Localization to Project-Level Context
sources.borrow: separate repository comprehension, navigation, and confirmation stages
sources.boundary: multi-agent end-to-end results do not isolate the value of any one G01 ranking component

sources.title: A Quantitative and Qualitative Evaluation of LLM-Based Explainable Fault Localization
sources.borrow: tool-mediated repository navigation plus a small set of evidence-backed explanations
sources.boundary: AutoFL method-level accuracy is not directly comparable with G01 file-level MRR

sources.title: CoRNStack: High-Quality Contrastive Data for Better Code Retrieval and Reranking
sources.borrow: a pinned 137M code-specific bi-encoder as an independent semantic retrieval channel
sources.boundary: Stack v2 training overlap is plausible for public BugsInPy repositories; exact-match filtering does not establish semantic decontamination

sources.title: CodeRankEmbed model card
sources.borrow: MIT-licensed 8K SentenceTransformers inference contract
sources.boundary: pin and hash the model revision and audit custom remote code before execution

sources.title: CoRet: Improved Retriever for Code Editing
sources.borrow: AST-sized chunks enriched with file hierarchy and call-graph context
sources.boundary: trained Python retriever results do not directly establish BugsInPy file-level gains

sources.title: Reformulate, Retrieve, Localize: Agents for Repository-Level Bug Localization
sources.borrow: extract identifiers, code snippets, stack traces and error messages before BM25 retrieval
sources.boundary: workshop results use bug reports rather than authenticated failure-log queries; ARE should preserve the raw query as an independent channel

sources.title: Taming System Complexity: Demystifying Software Engineering Agents in Diagnosing Linux Kernel Faults
sources.borrow: directory-aware candidate expansion, potential-cause expansion, and deterministic rank merging
sources.boundary: Linux-kernel results motivate mechanisms only; directory expansion should activate only after a G01 reach diagnostic

sources.title: Agentless: Demystifying LLM-based Software Engineering Agents
sources.borrow: hierarchical file-to-symbol localization and fusion of LLM and embedding retrieval
sources.boundary: end-to-end SWE-bench repair outcomes are not comparable with G01 file-ranking metrics

sources.title: FlexFL: Flexible and Effective Fault Localization with Open-Source Large Language Models
sources.borrow: combine heterogeneous first-stage fault-localization signals before LLM verification
sources.boundary: SBFL requires reproducible test coverage and belongs in a separate execution-evidence cycle

sources.title: Hierarchical Reward Modeling for Fault Localization in Large Code Repositories
sources.borrow: task-specific reward scoring over multiple sampled hierarchical localization answers
sources.boundary: a 7B reward model and multi-sample inference are not justified before cheaper evidence channels are tested

sources.title: Improving LLM-Based Fault Localization with External Memory and Project Context
sources.borrow: static project summaries and explicitly versioned dynamic debugging memory
sources.boundary: benchmark use requires a strict temporal and label-independence boundary for every memory item

sources.title: Structured Output
sources.borrow: provider JSON mode through response_format json_object, followed by local closed-schema validation
sources.boundary: JSON mode guarantees JSON formatting, not application-level candidate membership; invalid values still fail without repair

sources.title: SweRank: Software Issue Localization with Code Ranking
sources.borrow: task-specific issue-localization bi-encoder as a controlled replacement for CodeRankEmbed
sources.boundary: reported SWE-bench and LocBench results do not establish G01 effectiveness and public-repository training overlap remains plausible

sources.title: SweRankEmbed-Small model card
sources.borrow: 137M normalized embedding inference contract compatible with the existing bounded semantic runtime
sources.boundary: CC-BY-NC-4.0 permits the private research ablation but is not an assumed commercial product license

sources.title: Late Code Chunking: A Code Chunking Strategy for Repository-Level Code Completion
sources.borrow: separate compact retrieval representation from late comprehension context and test asymmetric query/chunk sizing
sources.boundary: code-completion results motivate a later representation ablation, not an immediate fault-localization claim

sources.title: Improving Code Localization with Repository Memory
sources.borrow: temporally bounded commit and issue memory plus module-functionality summaries
sources.boundary: post-failure history can reveal benchmark labels and must be excluded by an auditable cutoff

sources.title: FuseSearch: Learning Adaptive Parallel Execution for Efficient Code Localization
sources.borrow: measure unique information gain per tool call and adapt exploration breadth in a later graph-search cycle
sources.boundary: the published gain depends on a trained 4B interactive search policy and is not a drop-in static reranker

sources.title: Enhancing LLM-based Fault Localization with a Functionality-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework
sources.borrow: derive a concise failing-functionality description from failed-test and stack-trace evidence before dense code retrieval
sources.boundary: Defects4J method-level results do not establish G01 file-level gains; r57 must retain the authenticated raw query and a deterministic invalid-summary fallback

sources.title: BLAgent: Agentic RAG for File-Level Bug Localization
sources.borrow: independent structural and behavioral query retrieval before bounded file-level candidate merging
sources.boundary: SWE-bench Lite scores do not transfer to BugsInPy; r60 borrows only the dual-query acquisition mechanism and is not a BLAgent replication

sources.title: CeQe: Grounding Lexical Retrieval in Semantic Evidence
sources.borrow: improve lexical candidate supply by giving BM25 vocabulary-matched evidence instead of relying only on downstream reranking
sources.boundary: BEIR document results do not establish bug-localization gains; ARE r60 uses previously sealed functionality summaries rather than reproducing CE-QE's cross-encoder attribution
